turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict each candidate's largest SHG tensor
component |d_ij|, then select the 5 candidates whose |d_ij| is CLOSEST to 20
pm/V.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, closest first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
Given the dataset, the most reliable strategy is to match candidates to structurally analogous training compounds:

**Key observations:**
- The training set contains a large family of Li/Mg/Ga/Se and Li/Zn/Ga/Se quaternary selenides with |d_ij| values clustered around 12–35 pm/V, e.g. Li1Mg1Ga1Se3 (20.4–25.1), Li3Mg2Ga1Se5 (16.7–27.9), Li2Zn2Ga2Se6 (7.8–31.7), Li2Mg3Ga2Se7 (12.3–19.0).
- Candidates c008–c013 (Li2Zn1Ga2Se5) and c094–c099 (Li2Mg1Ga2Se5) are direct structural/chemical analogs of these families — polar monoclinic cells with nearly identical lattice parameters (~6.4–6.8 Å, ~3.9 Å, ~9.5 Å). Their SHG response should fall near the middle of that family's range (~17–23 pm/V), i.e., very close to 20.
- Other candidates are clearly off-target: alkali halide/borate-type structures (c040–c045, c054, c084–c086) will be very small (<5 pm/V, like Rb2Sr2Cl6 = 0.37); telluride/arsenide compounds (c038, c090, c066) will be very large (44–87 pm/V); SiC polytypes (c024–c029) and cubic zincblende-like compounds (c027, c037, c059) are centrosymmetric in character or high-symmetry with moderate-to-high values not near 20.

**Predictions for the closest matches (estimated |d_ij|):**
- c094 (Li2Mg1Ga2Se5): ≈ 20 pm/V — lies centrally in the Li/Mg/Ga/Se response range
- c097: ≈ 19–21 pm/V
- c096: ≈ 20–22 pm/V
- c010 (Li2Zn1Ga2Se5): ≈ 20–22 pm/V (Li/Zn/Ga/Se analogs bracket 19–24)
- c098: ≈ 21–23 pm/V

These five candidates, being near-duplicate polar structures of the Li–Mg/Zn–Ga–Se family whose training analogs average almost exactly 20 pm/V, are the best matches to the target.

Final: c094, c097, c096, c010, c098
